RWI Zimbabwe Human Rights Capacity Development Programme 2024- 2026

description.narrative: The Programmes overall objective is to contribute to enhanced enjoyment of constitutional rights in Zimbabwe. That all Zimbabweans equally have a greater enjoyment and protection of human rights through capable institutions which have the means to apply international human rights standards, as reflected in the Zimbabwean Constitution, in their law-, decision- and policy-making as well as practices thus represents the Programmes overall vision of success.

Det nya programmet syftar till att bidra till ett ökat åtnjutande av konstitutionella rättigheter i Zimbabwe genom lagstiftning, politik, praxis och beslutsfattande som i allt högre grad bygger på internationella normer och principer för mänskliga rättigheter, som återspeglas i Zimbabwes konstitution.

The programme aims at contributing to enhanced enjoyment of constitutional rights in Zimbabwe, through legislation, policies, practices and decision-making being increasingly informed by international human rights standards and principles, as reflected in the Constitution of Zimbabwe.

2024
• Increased interaction on human rights issues between University-based Law Clinics and stakeholders (governmental and non-governmental) working on access to justice in Zimbabwe.
• Enhanced community-based human rights outreach programmes by academic partner institutions through the University Law Clinics.
• Increased number of research papers and policy briefs on the nexus between human rights and the environment, as well as increased opportunities among Zimbabwean researchers and other key stakeholders to exchange experiences and best practices on environment and climate change, through the Annual Research Symposium on Human Rights.
• Increased availability of human rights refence material, including books, periodicals, reference manuals and training tools at academic partner institutions, ZHCR, ZGC and ZPCS.
• Increased research capacity within ZGC through the Training on Human Rights Research, Policy Brief and Advocacy Paper Development.
• Increased awareness in Zimbabwe about the role and mandate of ZGC through support to outreach activities reaching approximately 4 800 people.
• Increased knowledge and skills within ZHRC on how to apply human rights standards in practice, in particular towards strengthening the commissions capacity on report writing, as well as on monitoring and inspections.
• Enhanced structured dialogue and joint initiatives between ZHRC and ZPCS through human rights trainings carried out by ZHRC for recruit correctional officers at ZPCS, an outreach activity supported by the Programme.
• Increased knowledge and skills within ZPCS on how to apply international prison standards in their operations, as a result of Training of Trainers (ToT) and the Human Rights Leadership Trainings (HRLT).
• Increased interaction on human rights, gender equality, and anti-corruption between ZHRC, ZGC, ZACC and other main stakeholders via a policy dialogue led by the three independent commissions.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
